messages:
acme-sre: hitting a weird combo — streaming SSE connection drops mid-response, client then reconnects but server immediately returns a 429 and the customer's token ledger shows extra tokens charged for the aborted stream. repro steps below, can someone look?

Asha: sorry you're seeing that — can you paste the original request headers and the exact sequence (connect -> partial data -> 429)?

acme-sre: pasted excerpt:
```
GET /v1/stream?model=rw-instruct-13B HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-xyz
Accept: text/event-stream
Last-Event-ID: 
```
Then we got about ~420 tokens of output (events streamed), connection reset by client (mobile network flapped), client reconnected within 6s with the same auth token and Last-Event-ID set to the last event id we received. Immediately on reconnect we got an HTTP/1.1 429 with these headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-usage-tokens: 845
```
But customer billing report shows ~1250 tokens billed — overshoot of ~400 tokens.

Diego: interesting, two hypotheses: (1) token accounting is updated from in-flight buffers on disconnect and then double-counted when reconciling, (2) reconnect is being treated as a fresh request and the remainder of the streamed response is being generated then later billed separately.

Marta: can you share the exact usage event IDs or invoice IDs? We need to trace ledger entries to see where the extra tokens came from.

acme-sre: invoice id INV-9001 attached (sent via support ticket), sample usage entries: 2026-05-04T14:02:23Z stream_start token_count=0, 2026-05-04T14:02:25Z stream_partial token_count=420, 2026-05-04T14:02:30Z reconnect attempt, 2026-05-04T14:02:31Z 429 returned, 2026-05-04T14:03:00Z usage_event token_count=1250 (final).

Ken: can I try to repro from our lab using a flaky TCP simulator? acme-sre, do you have the Last-Event-ID values your client sets?

acme-sre: yes, they set Last-Event-ID: evt_20260504_140225. I can share a trace if needed.

Diego: quick telemetry check — I pulled the request logs for that token: we see a stream session open id session_0x7a, partial frames flushed in 3 chunks then a connection teardown at 6s. There was an auth refresh event from the auth service 2s after teardown for the same API key (rotated by client's infra). Our streamer retries queued work for the session on reconnect, and the rate limiter saw the new connection as a fresh session and allowed generation up to remaining quota, but the ledger reconciliation step after finalization merged the in-flight and final tallies incorrectly. That could create double-counting.

Asha: ok that matches hypothesis (1). Two immediate asks: (1) can you produce a minimal repro so we can run it locally? (2) For the customer, issue a temporary credit while we root cause.

acme-sre: repro recipe: start SSE stream, let server emit 300 tokens, force client TCP close (e.g., `tc qdisc` netem loss 100% for 100ms), reconnect with Last-Event-ID set to last seen, observe 429 midstream and ledger mismatch. I can reproduce on linux + node fetch.

Ken: repro attempt notes: I ran a loop where client crashes and reconnects with same key. I see two issues: our rate limiter currently doesn't attach a stable session id to reconnects when Last-Event-ID is present — so the new connection is treated as new allocation (and may exhaust remaining limit and send 429), while backend async accounting merges both session usages at finalize. Also the 429 lacks `x-session-resume` header to tell client whether it's safe to resume or must restart.

Diego: good catch. Adding `x-session-resume: allowed|denied` and including `session-id` in the 429 would let clients decide to resume vs restart. Put a tentative patch in the rate limiter to associate Last-Event-ID with session metadata and gate generation on aggregated in-flight tokens.

Marta: for billing — issue a provisional credit for the delta of ~400 tokens and flag invoice INV-9001 as disputed. I'll prepare the credit note once Support confirms amount.

Asha: internal action items: Diego to prototype rate-limiter fix + 429 header changes; Ken to stress test client resumption behavior against flaky networks; Marta to hold credit until we confirm. I'll own customer comms.

Diego: quick repro patch diff (high-level):
```
- if (newConnection) allocateQuota();\n+ if (LastEventID && sessionExists(LastEventID)) resumeSession(LastEventID) else allocateQuota();
```
Also add ledger flags so finalizeAccounting(sessionId, isResumed) deducts only delta not full stream again.

Ken: test results from lab: with patched resume logic, client reconnects and receives `HTTP/1.1 200` with `x-session-resume: allowed` and no double billing. Without patch we reproduce the overshoot. Sharing my test harness script in the ticket.

acme-sre: thanks — customers want ETA on fix and whether they need to rotate keys or change clients.

Asha: ETA: hotfix to rate limiter and headers today (small change), follow-up to update ledger reconciliation tomorrow. No forced key rotation required. Workaround for clients: if you get a midstream 429, do not assume tokens were consumed for the remainder — open a support ticket and include Last-Event-ID. We will send a `x-session-offset` header in the 429 in the hotfix to indicate where accounting stopped.

ingest-bot: Deployment scheduled: canary rollout to 10% at 2026-05-05T02:00Z, full rollout at 2026-05-05T04:00Z if metrics stable.

Marta: credit issued: 400 token-equivalent refunded to INV-9001, note attached. Please confirm and we'll close dispute.

acme-sre: confirmed refund received, thanks team. leaving logs/trace with you for postmortem.

Asha: closing loop: follow-up postmortem to cover telemetry gaps and ensure `x-session-resume` and `x-session-offset` docs added to Streaming API.
